title: Continuous integral operations isolate one pivot on a Stonean base
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with its valuation topology and integer ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $P$ be compact Hausdorff, totally disconnected and extremally disconnected, with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. For every $n,m\ge0$ and every entrywise continuous $F:P\to\operatorname{Mat}_{(n+1)\times(m+1)}(E)$, there are maps $L:P\to\operatorname{GL}_{n+1}(\mathcal O_E)$ and $U:P\to\operatorname{GL}_{m+1}(\mathcal O_E)$ whose entries and inverse entries are continuous after inclusion into $E$, such that $(LFU)_{0,j+1}=0$ for all $j<m$ and $(LFU)_{i+1,0}=0$ for all $i<n$. The lower-right block is unrestricted. Empty $P$, zero matrices, ties and varying zero loci are included.

proof.text: For a compact Hausdorff Stonean space $P$ and any compact Hausdorff source $X$ mapping continuously and surjectively to $P$, use [det-pe-stonean-projective] to choose a continuous section. If their universes differ, lift both spaces to the common maximum universe; the ULift homeomorphisms transport compactness, the Hausdorff property and extremal disconnectedness, and transport the section back. This is implemented by the private proved stonean_section helper.

For continuous $a,b:P\to E$ with $|a|\le|b|$, the equation space $Z=\{(p,t)\in P\times\mathcal O_E:a(p)=b(p)t\}$ is closed by continuity of the two sides. The integer ring is compact Hausdorff by [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower], its product with $P$ is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact], and $Z$ is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. Projection is surjective: take $a(p)/b(p)$ when $b(p)\ne0$, and zero otherwise, when the bound forces $a(p)=0$. A section gives continuous integral $q$ satisfying $a=bq$. This proves bounded_division.

To select a maximum of a finite nonempty family of continuous real functions $f_i$, put the finite index set $I$ in the discrete topology and form $Z=\{(p,i):\forall j, f_j(p)\le f_i(p)\}$. Evaluation $(p,i)\mapsto f_i(p)$ is continuous because $I$ is discrete, so $Z$ is closed in compact Hausdorff $P\times I$. Every finite family has a maximum, making projection surjective. A section gives a continuous index label for a maximum. Apply this to the norms of all $(n+1)(m+1)$ entries. This proves continuous_max_label and handles ties and common zeros without clopen closure iteration.

Let the selected index be $(r(p),c(p))$. Row and column permutation matrices associated to the swaps $(0,r(p))$ and $(0,c(p))$ give $A=SFT$ with every entry bounded in norm by $h=A_{00}$. Their entries and inverse entries factor through the finite discrete index label, so they are continuous. Permutation-matrix multiplication computes $A_{ij}=F_{(0,r)(i),(0,c)(j)}$.

Use bounded division separately to obtain continuous integral $q_i,t_j$ such that $A_{i+1,0}=h q_i$ and $A_{0,j+1}=h t_j$. For a column vector $q$, the matrix $N(q)$ with entries $N(q)_{i+1,0}=q_i$ and all other entries zero satisfies $N(q)N(t)=0$. Thus $R=I+N(-q)$ and $C=(I+N(-t))^{\mathsf T}$ are integral invertible matrices, with inverse obtained by changing plus to minus. Their entries and inverse entries are continuous.

The formulas $(RA)_{0j}=A_{0j}$, $(RA)_{i+1,j}=A_{i+1,j}-q_iA_{0j}$, $(BC)_{i0}=B_{i0}$ and $(BC)_{i,j+1}=B_{i,j+1}-B_{i0}t_j$ show that $RAC$ has zero first row and column except at the pivot. Take $L=RS$ and $U=TC$. Continuity of products follows entrywise by finite sums; inverse products use the reverse order. No assertion is made about the lower-right block, and no division by a zero scalar occurs.
